documents.title: Terms of Service
documents.content:
1. Acceptance of Terms

By accessing and using the CloudAlls digital ecosystem, client portal, or associated APIs, you agree to be bound by these Terms of Service. If you do not agree, please disconnect from our infrastructure immediately.

2. Enterprise License & Usage

CloudAlls grants you a limited, non-exclusive, non-transferable license to access our proprietary software. You are strictly prohibited from reverse-engineering, decompiling, or attempting to extract the source code of our AI models or backend architecture.

3. Payment & Billing Cycles

All enterprise SaaS subscriptions and retainer invoices are due within Net 15 days of issuance. Failure to settle accounts may result in automated suspension of portal access and API routing.

4. Limitation of Liability

CloudAlls shall not be liable for any indirect, incidental, special, consequential, or punitive damages, including loss of profits, data, or business goodwill, arising out of your use of our software ecosystem.

documents.title: Privacy & Data Policy
documents.content:
1. Global Compliance Standard

CloudAlls is fully compliant with the European Union General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and the India Digital Personal Data Protection Act (DPDP). We treat your personal and corporate data with the highest level of cryptographic security.

2. Data Collection & Telemetry

We collect essential telemetry data, IP addresses, browser footprints, and account credentials necessary to provide you with secure access to our portal. We never sell your personal data to third-party data brokers.

3. Data Storage & Encryption

All sensitive information, including litigation notes, passwords, and API keys, are encrypted at rest using AES-256-CBC encryption. Active databases are housed in ISO 27001-certified data centers across Mumbai and Frankfurt.

4. Your Rights (Data Subject Requests)

Under global privacy laws, you have the "Right to be Forgotten". You may request the export, modification, or complete deletion of your personal data from our servers. Please use the DSR Form located in this Legal Center to initiate a formal request.

documents.title: Cookie & Tracking Policy
documents.content:
1. Session Management

Cookies are small text files stored on your device. They are essential for maintaining secure user sessions and preventing Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) attacks.

2. Essential vs. Non-Essential Cookies
  • Essential Cookies: Used for authenticating your login and keeping your session secure. The portal cannot function without these.
  • Analytics Cookies: We use anonymized telemetry (without storing PII) to monitor dashboard performance and page load speeds.
3. Managing Your Preferences

You can instruct your browser to refuse all cookies. However, if you do not accept essential session cookies, you will be unable to log into the Admin or Client dashboards.

documents.title: Security & SLA Matrix
documents.content:
1. Uptime Guarantee

We guarantee a 99.9% uptime for all enterprise-tier clients. Scheduled maintenance will be communicated at least 48 hours in advance via the internal broadcasting system.

2. Incident Response

In the event of a critical Severity 1 (P1) outage, our NOC (Network Operations Center) guarantees a preliminary response and diagnostic initiation within 15 minutes.

3. Penetration Testing

Our infrastructure undergoes bi-annual third-party penetration testing. Executive summaries of these reports are available to Enterprise clients under a signed NDA.

documents.title: Acceptable Use Policy
documents.content:
1. Prohibited Activities

Users of the CloudAlls network may not engage in activities that are illegal, infringe on the rights of others, or interfere with our infrastructure. This includes, but is not limited to: DDoS attacks, malware distribution, phishing, and cryptojacking.

2. API Rate Limiting

To protect network integrity, all API endpoints are strictly rate-limited. Intentional attempts to bypass these limits will result in immediate API key revocation and permanent IP bans.

documents.title: Modern Slavery & Ethics
documents.content:
1. UN Global Compact

CloudAlls supports the Ten Principles of the United Nations Global Compact on human rights, labor, environment, and anti-corruption.

2. Supply Chain Integrity

We maintain a zero-tolerance approach to modern slavery and are committed to complying with the UK Modern Slavery Act 2015 in all global dealings.

documents.title: Web Accessibility Statement (WCAG)
documents.content:
CloudAlls is continuously actively taking steps to improve the accessibility of our corporate ecosystem and the software platforms we build for our enterprise clients. We are committed to adhering to the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.1 Level AA standards.

Current Architectural Measures
  • Semantic HTML: We utilize strict, semantic HTML5 structure to ensure seamless parsing by screen readers and assistive technologies.
  • Color Contrast: All brand colors and UI elements are heavily audited to meet required WCAG contrast ratios for visually impaired users.
  • Keyboard Navigation: The CloudAlls admin and client dashboards are fully navigable using keyboard-only inputs, without requiring a mouse.
  • Reduced Motion: We respect the OS-level prefers-reduced-motion media query, automatically disabling heavy parallax or structural animations for sensitive users.
Feedback & Support

Accessibility is an ongoing engineering effort. If you encounter any barriers while using our platforms, or require an alternative format for our documentation, please contact our compliance team immediately.

Accessibility Operations Desk

frameworks.authority: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology / Parliament of India
frameworks.scope_summary: India’s digital personal-data framework. Applicability, commencement, notices, rights, transfers, and obligations depend on the facts, notified provisions, and applicable rules.

frameworks.authority: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
frameworks.scope_summary: Rules and implementation detail should be reviewed with the Act and the organization’s processing activities before relying on them.
Cybersecurity incident handling, reporting, logging, and technical controls may apply according to the organization, system, incident, and current CERT-In directions.

frameworks.framework_name: UK GDPR and Data Protection Act 2018
frameworks.scope_summary: UK personal-data processing requires a scoped assessment of lawful basis, transparency, minimisation, rights, security, retention, processors, and international transfers.
Cookies, similar technologies, electronic marketing, and communications require a fact-specific review of notice, consent, exemptions, and record keeping.
Businesses should substantiate privacy and security representations and maintain safeguards appropriate to the nature of the data they hold. US requirements also vary by sector, state, and activity.

frameworks.framework_name: California Consumer Privacy Act / California Privacy Rights Act
frameworks.scope_summary: California privacy rights and business obligations depend on thresholds, data categories, purposes, consumer status, and the organization’s role.

frameworks.authority: National Institute of Standards and Technology
frameworks.scope_summary: NIST AI RMF is voluntary guidance for managing AI risks and incorporating trustworthiness into AI design, development, use, and evaluation. It is not a legal certification.
Principles-based guidance covering human rights, labour, environment, and anti-corruption. It is not a CloudAlls legal certification or a substitute for local law.

frameworks.framework_name: Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights
frameworks.authority: United Nations Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights
frameworks.scope_summary: The Protect, Respect and Remedy framework is a global reference for preventing and addressing adverse human-rights impacts involving business activity.

frameworks.framework_name: Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence
frameworks.scope_summary: A global normative reference for human dignity, human rights, fairness, transparency, environmental responsibility, and accountable AI governance.
